← Sonograph

A collection for listening

The initial listening curation selected 109 active patterns: 89 low-motion, redundant, strongly clipped or weakly articulated entries removed from browsing, and 16 new musical constructions added. Three against five and The final boss remain. Gentler contrasting sounds remain too.

New pieces use note attacks, releases, and real rests. Pitch still comes from the graph; amplitude can now have its own envelope. Some pieces interlock, some change harmony, some bend timbre, and some use sound particles or plucked strings. Next pattern gives these and the stronger existing pieces more weight while continuing to avoid the last 16 families.

Marshmallow motor

Equation and sound construction
y = [−2.5+9.5A+3sin(3θ)(1−A²)]/11.4
A = (sinθ+a sin(3θ))/√(1+a²+2a cos(2θ))

t=(x+8)/16; u=(x+8)/2; θ=2πu+0.28sin(4πu); a=0.545+0.12sin(2πt). A is the imaginary component of the normalized vector sum exp(iθ)+a exp(3iθ). Its rotating harmonics fold each arch into rounded shoulders; changing a gently reshapes those shoulders across the scan. Because a is below 0.7, the normalizing denominator stays above 0.3 and cannot create a break. The large arch reaches pitch anchors −12 and +7 semitones, separated by an octave and a fifth; an additional third-harmonic curl opens between them. Eight cycles cross the graph. Loudness E=0.4+0.6[(1+cos(2θ))/2]³ creates rounded accents and never reaches silence. Harmonic FM ratio 1 uses index 0.3+0.8(1−A²), opening the reed-like sound during bends. All pitch and timbre functions are smooth, with no clipped plateaus or step boundaries. Root=164.8138 Hz. Vivid uses pitch f=root·2^(11.4y/12), so the entire unbroken graph, including every ripple, drives the audible pitch. The amplitude stays positive throughout the interior; only the transport's short start and end fades reach silence. There is one voice and no backing drum track. Seed selects the key and the stated shape parameter where applicable. Both scan speeds traverse the same curve. Original keeps its existing pitch mapping and voice synthesis.

Ribbon racer

Equation and sound construction
y = [(1−S)Mₙ+SMₙ₊₁+3sin(2πr)sin²(πr)]/11.4
S = 6v⁵−15v⁴+10v³; v = clamp((r−0.55)/0.45,0,1)

u=2(x+8); n=⌊u⌋; r=frac(u); M=(-12, -5, 0, 7, 4, 2, 0, -5, -8, -3, 4, 9, 7, 4, 2, -12), indexed modulo 16. A major-pentatonic phrase runs twice across the graph. Each cell holds its starting note through r=0.55, then slides into the next using a quintic interpolant. S has zero first and second derivatives at both ends; the additional pitch curl and its first two derivatives also vanish at the cell boundaries. Consequently y, y′ and y″ match across every join, including the motif repeat. The line has no jumps or missing intervals. Loudness E=0.3+0.7[(1+cos(2πr))/2]³ stays positive and smooth across cell joins. A pure sine gives the connected scoops a slide-whistle character. The final point returns to the opening tonic. Root=146.8324 Hz. Vivid uses pitch f=root·2^(11.4y/12), so the entire unbroken graph, including every ripple, drives the audible pitch. The amplitude stays positive throughout the interior; only the transport's short start and end fades reach silence. There is one voice and no backing drum track. Seed selects the key and the stated shape parameter where applicable. Both scan speeds traverse the same curve. Original keeps its existing pitch mapping and voice synthesis.

Taffy tornado

Equation and sound construction
y = [2+8sin(φ+βsin(2φ))+4sin(5φ)/(2+cosφ)]/11.4
φ = 2π[6t+0.16sin(4πt)]

t=(x+8)/16; β=0.275+0.12sin(2πt). Six broad waves carry nested phase bends and a fivefold rational ripple. The denominator 2+cosφ is at least 1, so the ripple cannot create poles, breaks or clipped asymptotes. The phase clock remains increasing: d[6t+0.16sin(4πt)]/dt≥6−0.64π>0. The slowly changing phase depth reshapes the middle of the scan before returning home. Loudness E=0.38+0.62[(1+cos(2φ+π/3))/2]² adds rounded, offset accents without silence. The hollow harmonic voice keeps the lower swoops warm and the smaller ripples audible. The pitch is one analytic function, with no note gates or discrete pitch table. Root=174.6141 Hz. Vivid uses pitch f=root·2^(11.4y/12), so the entire unbroken graph, including every ripple, drives the audible pitch. The amplitude stays positive throughout the interior; only the transport's short start and end fades reach silence. There is one voice and no backing drum track. Seed selects the key and the stated shape parameter where applicable. Both scan speeds traverse the same curve. Original keeps its existing pitch mapping and voice synthesis.

Jelly gears

Equation and sound construction
y = [Mₙ + 7Bₐ(r)sin(πr)]/11.4
Bₐ(r) = (1−a²)sin(2πr)/(1+a²−2a cos(2πr))

n=⌊1.5(x+8)⌋; r=frac(1.5(x+8)); a=0.555; M=(-12, -5, 0, -3, -8, -5, 2, -12), repeated every eight cells. Cells 16…19 raise M by 12 semitones. B is the sine component of the unit-circle map (z−a)/(1−az), z=exp(2πir); its nonuniform phase creates an asymmetric elastic curve. The lead uses gate 0.91, decay 1.1 and harmonic FM ratio 1 with index 0.35+1.15sin²(πr). A glass reply enters after eight cells on n mod 4=3: clock offset 0.22 graph units, pitch Mₙ+7−3sin(πr), gate 0.6, decay 2.5, weight 0.38. The shifted reply uses its own n and r. No percussion layer. Root=196.0000 Hz. In Vivid, pitch f=root·2^(11.4y/12); the displayed curve directly controls pitch, including every bend. Each active cell has envelope min(1,r/0.055)exp(−decay·r)clamp((gate−r)/0.09,0,1), multiplied by its stated gain. Undefined intervals are silent rests. A final amplitude fade starts at x=7.78 and all voices stop at x=7.9. Seed changes select key; Jelly gears also varies a. Both scan speeds traverse the same functions. Original uses the existing legacy pitch mapping.

Divisor dance

Equation and sound construction
Hₙ(r) = [Σd∣n, d≤6 sin(2πdr)/d]/[Σd∣n, d≤6 1/d]
y₁ = [Pₙ+4Hₙ(r)]/11.4

n=⌊2(x+8)⌋+1; r=frac(2(x+8)); τ(n) counts all positive divisors of n; S=(0, 3, 5, 7, 10). Pₙ=S[(τ(n)−1) mod 5]+12(⌊(n−1)/8⌋ mod 2)−12. Each cell adds a normalized sum of only those harmonics 1…6 that divide n, giving primes a smooth shape and composites finer internal ripples. The normalization keeps |H|≤1. Lead gate 0.88, decay 1.3; multiples of four have gain 1, other cells 0.82. On n mod 4=0, a low triangular voice answers at y₂=[S[(τ(n)−1) mod 5]−24+3exp(−16r)]/11.4; gate 0.62, decay 3, weight 0.46. Eight-cell blocks alternate register, while divisor structure changes the internal wiggle. Root=164.8138 Hz. In Vivid, pitch f=root·2^(11.4y/12); the displayed curve directly controls pitch, including every bend. Each active cell has envelope min(1,r/0.055)exp(−decay·r)clamp((gate−r)/0.09,0,1), multiplied by its stated gain. Undefined intervals are silent rests. Technique references

These sources informed the mechanisms. Melodies, event schedules and arrangements are original Sonograph compositions.

  • Steve Reich: Piano Phase - composer notes - Two players repeating a motif at slightly different speeds inspired Phase marimbas. The melody here is original.
  • Stanford: the Karplus-Strong algorithm - String waterfall uses seeded noise, a fractional feedback delay and low-pass averaging to create actual plucked-string tones.
  • Barry Truax: granular synthesis - Firefly cloud sums short overlapping chirplets under smooth windows, with seeded event density and pitch.
  • Stanford CCRMA: an introduction to FM - Robot vowels and Talking drums use changing modulation ratios and indices to give notes changing spectra.
  • Viznut: discovering novel computer music techniques - Bitwise arcade uses an original XOR-and-shift note selector inspired by algorithmic chip music; it does not copy a bytebeat tune.

What was trimmed

Simple waveform duplicates, isolated broad swells, long monotonic contours, several noisy untuned staircases, redundant phase studies, mostly clipped geometric curves, and the broken constant-output Fibonacci entry were removed from the active collection. Removing them does not erase their earlier seed definitions.
